ai-ethernet.definition: Ethernet-based AI networking systems — switches, fabric platforms, SDN control planes — that interconnect accelerators within and across clusters (Arista, Cisco).

architecture-ip.definition: Licensable processor / architecture IP — CPU and GPU cores, instruction sets — supplied to chip designers rather than as finished silicon (ARM, RISC-V).

cmp.definition: Chemical mechanical planarization — polishing the wafer flat between layers so lithography retains depth of focus. Step count scales with interconnect layers and with hybrid bonding in advanced packaging (Applied Materials, Ebara; Hwatsing domestically).

compute-memory.definition: Functional domain — the silicon and IP that perform computation and hold working data: merchant GPUs / CPUs, custom accelerators, memory and storage, the architecture and memory-interface IP they integrate, and the on-package / in-rack high-speed I/O that links them.

coupe-io.definition: Co-packaged optical I/O engines (e.g. TSMC COUPE) that integrate optical interconnect directly with compute silicon for energy-efficient scale-out bandwidth.

cpo-switch-asic.definition: Co-packaged-optics switch silicon and optical DSPs / retimers that drive optical links — Broadcom Tomahawk photonics, Marvell optical DSP.

custom-asic.definition: Purpose-built AI accelerators and custom silicon designed for a specific buyer or workload — hyperscaler TPU / Trainium-class parts and the design houses (Broadcom, Marvell) that co-develop them. Distinct from stack.gpu-cpu (merchant general-purpose accelerators).

dci.definition: Long-haul and metro optical transport linking data centers — coherent DCI systems and transponders (Ciena-class).

deposition.definition: Thin-film addition — CVD, PVD, ALD and epitaxy — laying down the conductor, dielectric and barrier layers a device is built from. ALD share rises with each node as films thin toward atomic scale (Applied Materials, Lam Research, ASM International, Kokusai; Piotech and NAURA domestically).

design-manufacturing.definition: Functional domain — the design tools and front-end fabrication that bring a chip into existence: EDA software, advanced-node foundry manufacturing, and the capital equipment for wafer processing and advanced packaging. Enablers of compute rather than compute itself.

dry-etch.definition: Plasma etch systems that selectively remove material to transfer the patterned mask into the underlying film — conductor, dielectric and high-aspect-ratio etch. Step count scales with 3D structures (3D NAND, GAA), making it the largest WFE segment after lithography (Lam Research, TEL, Applied Materials; NAURA and AMEC domestically).

eda.definition: Electronic-design-automation tools — synthesis, place-and-route, verification, simulation — used to design every chip (Synopsys, Cadence, Siemens EDA).

fiber.definition: Optical fiber and cabling — the passive physical medium for optical interconnect, intra- and inter-data-center (Corning fiber).

foundry.definition: Front-end wafer fabrication at advanced process nodes — TSMC, Samsung Foundry, Intel Foundry. Where compute silicon is physically manufactured.

gpu-cpu.definition: General-purpose merchant AI compute silicon — data-center GPUs and host CPUs sold to any buyer (NVIDIA, AMD). Distinct from stack.custom-asic (accelerators purpose-built for a single buyer or workload).

high-speed-connectivity.definition: Connectivity-chip silicon at the scale-out / cluster level — retimers, active-cable, and fabric-link silicon connecting accelerators across nodes and racks (Credo, MACOM, Semtech, Astera Labs). The cluster-scale counterpart to stack.high-speed-io (the in-node / on-package view); an actor spanning both carries both positions.

high-speed-io.definition: On-package and in-rack data-movement silicon — SerDes, PCIe / CXL retimers and switches, CXL memory controllers — that links compute, memory, and peripherals at high bandwidth WITHIN a node or rack (Astera Labs, Credo). The in-rack view of connectivity silicon; its scale-out / cluster-level counterpart is stack.high-speed-connectivity (Interconnect & Optical). An actor whose products span both views carries both positions.

interconnect-optical.definition: Functional domain — the optical and network technology that connects accelerators across nodes and data centers: silicon photonics and co-packaged optics, optical modules and DSPs, scale-out connectivity silicon, AI Ethernet and DCI systems, optical EMS, and fiber.

ion-implant.definition: Dopant introduction — high-current, high-energy and medium-current implanters that set device electrical characteristics. A concentrated segment with few credible suppliers (Applied Materials, Axcelis; Wanye, NAURA and Hwatsing domestically).

liquid-cooling.definition: Thermal management for dense AI racks — cold plates, CDUs, immersion, heat-rejection — required once per-rack power exceeds air-cooling limits.

lithography.definition: Wafer patterning scanners and steppers — EUV, immersion and dry DUV, i-line — that project circuit patterns onto photoresist. The step that gates leading-edge node access and the tightest export-control chokepoint in the stack (ASML, Canon, Nikon; SMEE and SiCarrier domestically in China).

memory-interface-ip.definition: Licensable controller / PHY IP for memory interfaces (DDR / LPDDR / HBM) integrated into SoCs. The interface-IP tier feeding memory connectivity; distinct from stack.memory-storage (the memory devices themselves).

memory-storage.definition: Semiconductor memory and storage attached to compute — DRAM, HBM, NAND, enterprise SSD / HDD. The capacity-and-bandwidth tier feeding the accelerators.

optical-ems.definition: Precision contract manufacturing / EMS for optical and photonic assemblies — the build-side of the optical-module supply chain.

optical-modules.definition: Pluggable optical transceiver modules and their components (lasers, photodetectors), assembled from photonics and electronics — Coherent, Lumentum, InnoLight, AOI.

packaging-equipment.definition: Capital equipment for advanced packaging and 3D integration — hybrid bonders, thermal-compression bonders, back-end lithography / deposition — supplied to foundries and OSATs. Grouped with Design & Manufacturing as front-end / capital tooling, distinct from the back-end packaging SERVICE (stack.packaging-test).

packaging-substrate.definition: Functional domain — the back-end assembly and carriers that turn finished dies into deployable modules: advanced packaging and final test (CoWoS, fan-out, 3D stacking) plus the IC substrates and high-layer-count PCBs that carry the die to the board.

packaging-test.definition: Back-end assembly, advanced packaging (CoWoS, fan-out, 3D stacking), and final test — TSMC in-house packaging plus OSATs (ASE, Amkor). The throughput bottleneck for AI-accelerator output.

photoresist-track.definition: Coater-developer tracks that apply, bake and develop photoresist, clustered with the lithography scanner they feed. A near-monopoly step (TEL holds the overwhelming majority share; SCREEN and, domestically, Kingssemi are the alternatives). Distinct from the resist chemistry itself, which is aie:ChemicalSupplier territory (JSR, TOK, Shin-Etsu).

power-semi.definition: Power-conversion semiconductors and modules (SiC / GaN, VRMs, power stages) that deliver and regulate current to accelerators at rack and board level — Vicor, Power Integrations, Navitas.

power-thermal.definition: Functional domain — the power delivery and heat removal that keep dense AI racks operating: power-conversion semiconductors and modules (SiC / GaN, VRMs, power stages) and liquid-cooling systems (cold plates, CDUs, immersion). Neither is packaging; both gate deployable rack density.

process-control.definition: Metrology and inspection that measure and gate every other step — overlay and CD metrology, wafer and mask defect inspection, e-beam review. Yield-learning infrastructure rather than a transformation step, but conventionally counted inside WFE (KLA, Applied Materials, Lasertec; SkyVerse, Jingce and SiCarrier domestically).

seg.ai-infrastructure.definition: Datacenter AI silicon and the memory and interconnect around it — merchant accelerators, custom-ASIC design services, connectivity chips, and DRAM / HBM.

seg.autonomous-driving.definition: Automotive AI compute for perception and driving policy. Source members: NVIDIA, Qualcomm, Mobileye, TI; Horizon Robotics, Black Sesame and HiSilicon domestically.

seg.back-end-equipment.definition: Test and assembly tooling — testers, handlers, probers. Category and taggable concept at once. Deliberately NOT aligned to aie:stack.packaging-equipment, which means bonders and back-end litho; the disagreement is preserved rather than resolved (ADR 027 § SEG-003).

seg.cleaning.definition: Wafer surface preparation and contamination removal. Source members: SCREEN, Lam Research, TEL; ACM Research, NAURA and PNC Process domestically.

seg.cmp.definition: Chemical mechanical planarization. Source members: Applied Materials, Ebara; Hwatsing domestically.

seg.connectivity.definition: Data-movement silicon inside and between racks. The clearest case where the source's boundary differs from this project's: aie:StackTaxonomy splits the same companies across stack.high-speed-io (in-rack) and stack.high-speed-connectivity (cluster-scale), so the mapping is one-to-many (ADR 027 § SEG-003).

seg.deposition.definition: Thin-film deposition — CVD, PVD, ALD, epitaxy. Source members: Applied Materials, Lam Research, ASM International, Kokusai; Piotech and NAURA domestically.

seg.design-service.definition: Custom-ASIC design houses and design-service providers that co-develop silicon for a named buyer — Broadcom, Marvell, MediaTek, Alchip, GUC; VeriSilicon and Brite domestically.

seg.dram-hbm.definition: Datacenter memory — DRAM and high-bandwidth memory. Source members: Samsung, SK Hynix, Micron; CXMT, YMTC and SwaySure domestically.

seg.dry-etch.definition: Plasma etch systems. Source members: Lam Research, TEL, Applied Materials; NAURA and AMEC domestically.

seg.edge-ai.definition: AI silicon outside the datacenter — smartphone SoCs, autonomous-driving compute, and smart-cockpit processors. Has no aie:StackTaxonomy counterpart by design: edge silicon is not part of the AI datacenter hardware stack, so these actors carry a segment and a type but no stack position (ADR 027 Open Question 3).

seg.foundry.definition: Leading-edge contract wafer manufacturing. Category and taggable concept at once — the source carries no subcategory beneath it.

seg.gpu-accelerator.definition: Merchant datacenter AI compute silicon. Source members span NVIDIA and AMD against the full domestic Chinese cohort — Cambricon, Hygon, Moore Threads, Biren, MetaX, Iluvatar, Enflame, and the captive designs (HiSilicon, T-Head, Kunlunxin).

seg.hardware-components.definition: Board- and system-level content around the accelerator — optical modules, PCB and IC substrate, and power ICs and modules.

seg.hyperscalers.definition: The cloud and platform buyers whose capex drives the rest of the landscape. Category and taggable concept at once. The demand side of the segmentation — these actors carry no aie:hasStackPosition, since they consume the stack rather than occupy a position in it.

seg.ion-implant.definition: Dopant implantation systems. Source members: Applied Materials, Axcelis; Wanye, NAURA and Hwatsing domestically.

seg.lithography.definition: Wafer patterning scanners and steppers. Source members: ASML, Canon, Nikon; SMEE and SiCarrier domestically.

seg.optics-connectivity.definition: Optical modules and components. Source members: Coherent, Lumentum; Innolight and Eoptolink domestically.

seg.osat.definition: Outsourced assembly, packaging and test services. Category and taggable concept at once. Note the source places TSMC and Intel here as well as under Foundry — a company can hold both.

seg.pcb-substrate.definition: Printed circuit boards and IC substrates. Source members: Ibiden, Unimicron, Kinsus; Shengyi, Shennan, FastPrint, Dongshan, Wus, Victory Giant and Avary domestically — the largest single-segment domestic cohort in the source.

seg.photoresist-processing.definition: Coater-developer tracks feeding the lithography cell. Source members: TEL; Kingssemi and ACM Research domestically.

seg.power-ic.definition: Power management ICs and power modules feeding the rack. Source members: MPS, TI, Renesas, Infineon, Delta; JoulWatt, NCE Power, CR Micro and Megmeet domestically.

seg.process-control.definition: Metrology and defect inspection. Source members: KLA, Applied Materials, Lasertec; SiCarrier, SkyVerse and Jingce domestically.

seg.smart-cockpit.definition: In-cabin infotainment and cockpit-domain processors. Source members: Qualcomm, MediaTek; Rockchip, AutoChips, Black Sesame and Amlogic domestically.

seg.smartphone-soc.definition: Application processors with on-device AI acceleration. Source members: Qualcomm, MediaTek, Apple, Samsung; HiSilicon and UNISOC domestically.

seg.thermal-process.definition: Furnace, RTP and anneal systems. Source members: Applied Materials, TEL, Kokusai; NAURA and ACM Research domestically.

seg.wafer-fab-equipment.definition: Front-end process tooling, decomposed by step. Boundary-compatible with the aie:StackTaxonomy D6 domain added alongside it (ADR 027 § SEG-004), but tracked separately: the stack leaves are this project's own model and may diverge as other sources are landed.

siph-foundry.definition: Photonics-capable foundry processes (GlobalFoundries Fotonix, TSMC SiPh, Intel SiPh) that fabricate silicon-photonics ICs — the SiPh analogue of stack.foundry. Grouped under Interconnect & Optical (not Design & Manufacturing) because its output is exclusively optical interconnect silicon.

substrate-pcb.definition: IC package substrates (ABF organic, emerging glass-core) and high-layer-count PCBs that carry the die to the board — Ibiden, Unimicron, Shinko.

theme.ai-financing.definition: The capital-structure narrative of the AI buildout — vendor financing, GPU-backed debt, special-purpose vehicles, and circular flows where a supplier funds its own customers (the Burry thesis). An analyst / short narrative, not a tradable basket (no ETF), but graph-native: the project already models VCI, Apollo debt financing, and vendor-financing loops. Membership = an actor materially exposed to or structuring AI vendor / SPV financing.

theme.ai-power.definition: Electricity generation, grid, and on-site power as the binding constraint on AI data-center buildout — utilities / IPPs, gas turbines, transformers and switchgear, nuclear / SMR, and the facility-side power & thermal (liquid cooling) hardware that gates deployable rack density. The 2026 consensus-bottleneck theme; ETF: AIPO. Folds the nuclear / SMR and liquid-cooling sub-narratives.

theme.photonics.definition: Light replaces copper as the high-bandwidth interconnect backbone of AI data centers — silicon photonics, co-packaged optics, optical transceivers / modules and DSPs, the lasers and III-V materials that feed them, photonics-capable foundries, and optical EMS. Cross-cutting: spans materials makers (AXT, IQE), foundries (GlobalFoundries, X-FAB), laser / component vendors (Coherent, Lumentum, Sivers), and networking / ASIC players (Broadcom, Marvell). Dedicated ETFs: FOTO, LYTE, EUV. Membership = a defensible role in moving data with light, or supplying that stack (THM-004).

theme.physical-ai.definition: Embodied AI — humanoid robots, actuators, sensors, and the edge compute that runs them — as the next demand wave for AI silicon and an application surface beyond the data center. Record VC funding through 2026; analyst frameworks (Barclays two-wave).

theme.semicap.definition: The capital-equipment vendors that enable all AI silicon regardless of who wins at the chip level — lithography, deposition, etch, metrology, epitaxy, and test (ASML, Applied Materials, Lam Research, KLA, Teradyne, Advantest, Aixtron). The mature picks-and-shovels basket; ETFs: SMH, SOXX.

thermal-process.definition: Furnace, rapid-thermal and laser-anneal systems that drive oxidation, diffusion, dopant activation and film densification. Adjacent to deposition — vertical furnaces often serve both — so vendors commonly carry both positions (Applied Materials, TEL, Kokusai; NAURA and ACM Research domestically).

wafer-cleaning.definition: Wet and dry surface preparation between process steps — particle, residue and contamination removal that determines yield at every layer. Named 'wafer-cleaning' rather than 'cleaning' to keep it unambiguous against back-end part cleaning (SCREEN, Lam Research, TEL; ACM Research and PNC Process domestically).

wafer-fab-equipment.definition: Functional domain — the front-end capital equipment that turns a blank wafer into patterned silicon, decomposed by process step: patterning (lithography, photoresist track), material removal (dry etch, CMP, cleaning), material addition (deposition, thermal process), doping (ion implant), and the metrology / inspection that gates each step. Distinct from stack.packaging-equipment (back-end / advanced-packaging tooling, D2), which acts on singulated die rather than wafers, and from the test handlers grouped under stack.packaging-test (D3). Added by ADR 027 § SEG-004.
